item.title: OpenMandriva Alleges Contributor Sabotage After Repository Deletions and Package Obsoletions
item.content:encoded:
OpenMandriva Linux says contributor tried to sabotage the project — May Read

OpenMandriva says a former contributor attempted to sabotage the Linux distribution by deleting GitHub repositories and pushing an empty package that could have disrupted GNOME and Cosmic desktop packages for users. The contributor denies intending harm, while the project is restoring affected repositories and auditing for further unauthorized changes.

  • The OpenMandriva Linux project said it was targeted by an attempted internal sabotage following a dispute among contributors.
  • OpenMandriva maintainer AngryPenguin said Davide Beatrici deleted part of a repository the team had worked on for almost a decade after previously receiving administrative privileges to help migrate and mirror repositories to his private OneDev instance.
  • AngryPenguin said Beatrici also published an empty package in the Cooker repository that obsoleted packages for the GNOME and Cosmic desktop environments.
  • The OpenMandriva team said it is restoring deleted repositories and packages and conducting a full system audit for other unauthorized changes.
  • Beatrici rejected the sabotage claims in a statement to The Lunduke Journal, saying he did not intend to harm OpenMandriva or its users.
